notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.14_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.14.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.14.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **Bring your own relay.** Settings has a relay section, and it asks one
  question: the public relays, or one of yours. Leave it on the first and
  nothing changes — Ruze uses the free ones iroh ships with, which is what
  every copy has always done and what costs nobody anything. Pick the second
  and this device stops using those entirely — the reason to run your own
  relay is not wanting to depend on someone else's, so a quiet fallback to
  the public ones would have undone the point of the setting.

  The same question is offered on the welcome screen, closed by default,
  so that someone who already runs a relay never has a first session on
  somebody else's. It is one control in three places — settings, connection
  health, and first run — rather than three that can disagree.

  It applies the moment you press Save. No restart, unlike the sync-host
  port, because a relay is a URL you might get wrong on the first try and
  a setting you can only test by rebooting the app is one nobody tests.

  A relay is worth understanding before changing it. Two devices that can
  reach each other directly barely touch one — iroh treats the relay as a
  backup path and moves off it the moment a direct route opens. What always
  goes through it is finding each other in the first place, and everything
  else only when there is no direct route. Either way the relay carries
  ciphertext: it learns who is talking to whom and when, never what was
  said.

- **Mute yourself from the tray.** While you are in a voice channel the tray
  menu carries a Mute microphone checkmark, next to the call it belongs to and
  the entry that leaves it. The tray is where you reach for this precisely when
  Ruze is not the window in front of you, which is also why it is a checkmark
  rather than a label that flips between Mute and Unmute — it says what is true
  now instead of what clicking it would do.

- **Reply to a message.** Pick Reply on any message, or the arrow beside it,
  and the composer says who you are answering until you send or press Escape.
  The reply carries a quoted line of the original above it, which is a click
  away from the message itself — it scrolls there and flashes it, so you land
  on the line rather than near it.

  Being replied to is the one thing in a chat addressed to one person, so it
  is the one thing worth interrupting for. It has its own three-note chime, it
  marks the channel's badge with an @, and it raises a system notification when
  Ruze is not the window you are looking at. That last one has a switch in
  settings. Ordinary messages get none of it: a notification for every message
  in every channel is one nobody reads, and the first thing anyone does with it
  is turn the whole thing off, which would take the replies with it.

  A reply finds you on any of your devices, not just the one that wrote the
  message being answered.

### Fixed

- **Posting a message takes you to it.** On a phone it often did not: whether
  the list followed a new message was decided by measuring how far from the
  bottom you were *after* it had already been added, so any message taller than
  a couple of lines read as "you have scrolled away" the moment it arrived — and
  a wrapped paragraph on a narrow screen is exactly that. Your own messages now
  always win, whatever the measurement says, and the list settles after the
  keyboard has finished resizing the window rather than before.

- **A dialog scrolls when the window is shorter than it is.** On a short window
  the invite dialog showed its middle and nothing else — the opening paragraph
  cut off above, the buttons below the fold, and no way to reach either. Seven
  dialogs had no height limit; a centred dialog that outgrows the window
  overflows in both directions, and the half above the centre line cannot be
  scrolled to at all.

- **A video we cannot play opens in your browser instead of freezing the app.**
  On Linux, playback goes through GStreamer, whose codecs are separate packages
  a distribution may not have installed. Pressing play without them did not fail,
  it hung. Ruze now checks what is actually installed before it mounts a player,
  and where the answer is no the embed becomes a link out with the reason given.
  The Flatpak also carries a fuller codec set than before, so it should not come
  up there at all.

- **Joining a voice channel no longer closes the Android app.** Release builds
  minify, and two classes are reached only from Rust over JNI by name —
  nothing in Kotlin or the manifest calls them — so R8 could not see they were
  used and stripped them. Joining a call then looked for a method that was no
  longer there.

  What turned that into the app vanishing was a second bug behind it. A failed
  JNI call leaves the Java exception pending, and the code returned without
  clearing it; a pending exception takes the process down at the next JNI call
  from any thread, which during a call is the audio thread a few milliseconds
  later. So a service that failed to start did not report a failed start, it
  ended the app. Both halves are fixed: the classes are kept, and the
  exception is cleared on every path out.

  The same stripping had silently broken installing an update from inside the
  app, which is reached the same way.
